history.summary: Bhismaknagar is NOT an active temple - it is a ruined brick hill fort about 29-30 km south-east of Roing at Khatan/Koronu, ascribed to the Chutia kingdom that ruled the Sadiya region from the 11th to the 16th century CE; it formed part of the historical Sadhayapura capital region, possibly the fortified city of Doi-Thang (Wikipedia). Legend identifies it as the capital of King Bhismaka of the Mahabharata (father of Rukmini). ASI excavations in 1969-73 yielded terracotta plaques, decorative tiles, pottery and terracotta figurines, pointing to a sophisticated planned settlement with burnt-brick construction. It is a holy heritage site for the Idu Mishmis. DATING CONFLICT: some travel sources say 8th century, the official district site says circa 12th century AD; the 'Temple Complex' label is a misnomer - the site is fort ruins with no documented active worship. Coordinates are locality-level (Bhismaknagar, Koronu) - approximate.

town_description: Roing is the headquarters of the Lower Dibang Valley district, set on the plains below the Dibang hills near the Dibang River. It is the base for the Roing-Mayudia-Anini tourist circuit, the Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary and Sally Lake, and the ancient Bhismaknagar fort.
